purpose:
Request agreement to accept Pride in Place
Percy Main 10 year funding and act as the accountable body. To
understand the details of the programme
content:
Cabinet received a report in
respect of The Pride in Place Programme (PiPP).  Cabinet were advised that this is a
£1.5billion UK Government programme which delivers up to
£20million of funding and support over a 10 year period to
disadvantaged areas across the UK.
 
Cabinet were advised that one
of the areas to be allocated PiPP funding from the Government
covers parts of the Chirton and Percy Main and North Shields wards,
as was shown in the map at Appendix 1 to the report.  Cabinet were advised that the aim of the PiPP
funding is to regenerate disadvantaged neighbourhoods through
community-led decision making. 
Decisions on how and where the PiPP funding is spent will sit with
newly established ‘Neighbourhood Boards’, including the
‘Percy Main Neighbourhood Board’ (“the
Neighbourhood Board”) which is in the process of being
established.
 
The report advised Cabinet of
the arrangements that will be put in place by the Authority to
support the Neighbourhood Board, which as stated, will be
responsible for making decisions relating to the PiPP funding for
parts of the Chirton and Percy Main and North Sheilds wards
(“the Neighbourhood”).
 
Cabinet were advised that the
Government requires the Board to be led by an independent Chair,
and for the Board to include residents, local business members,
civil society and community organisation members.  The local Member of Parliament is also appointed
to the Board.  The Neighbourhood Board
will be supported by the Authority as the Board’s
“Accountable Body” because the Board has no legal
personality.
 
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to
 
(i)             
Authorise the Chief Finance Officer (Section 151
Officer) to take receipt of all Pride in Place Programme Funding
provided by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government, and
(ii)            
Note the areas of Chirton and Percy Main and North
Shields wards that have been allocated Pride in Place Programme
funding as shown in the map attached to the report, and
(iii)          
Note the appointment of Dame Norma Redfearn DBE as
the Independent Chair of the Percy Main Neighbourhood Board by the
Elected Mayor on behalf of the Authority and Sir Alan Campbell as
the Member of Parliament whose constituency includes the areas of
Chirton and Percy Main and North Shields included in the
Neighbourhood Board, and
(iv)          
Agree to the Authority becoming the Accountable Body
for the Percy Main Neighbourhood Board and to authorise the Chief
Finance Officer and the Interim Head of Law to take all necessary
steps to implement this decision, including, but not limited to,
drafting an Accountable Body Agreement for submission to the Percy
Main Neighbourhood Board for the Board’s agreement,
and
(v)            
Authorise the Interim Head of Law in consultation
with the Chair of the Percy Main Board to draft a Percy Main
Neighbourhood Decision-Making Process for submission to the
Neighbourhood Board for that Board’s agreement,
and
(vi)          
Authorise the Interim Head of Law in consultation
with the Chair of the Percy Main Neighbourhood Board to draft a
Code of Conduct for Members of the Board and Arrangements for
Dealing with Allegations of Breaches of the Code of Conduct
(‘Local Arrangements’) for submission to the
Neighbourhood Board for that Board’s agreement,
and
(vii)         
Authorise the Director of Customer, Digital and
Corporate Strategy in consultation with the Chief Finance Officer
and the Chair of the Percy Main Neighbourhood Board to approve the
submission of the Neighbourhood Board’s composition, boundary
confirmation, and the Neighbourhood Vision and Pride in Place
Investment Plans to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government, and
(viii)       
Authorise the Chief Finance Officer in consultation
with the Chair of the Percy Main Neighbourhood Board to develop and
embed appropriate processes for the Neighbourhood Board to seek
funding for its projects from the Pride in Place Programme funding
held by the Authority as the Neighbourhood Board’s
Accountable Body.
 
Reasons for the
Decision:
 
This will enable the
Neighbourhood Board to operate in accordance with the various
guides published by MHCLG including the ‘Pride in Place
Programme: governance and boundary guidance’ updated in March
2026.  The requirement for the
Neighbourhood Board to operate through the Authority as its
Accountable Body ensures that its decision-making will be in
accordance with the Guidance which states that: –
 
“Decision-making will be
led by the Neighbourhood Board, with the relevant local authority
in each place acting as the accountable body for the funds at the
start of the programme, with responsibility for ensuring that
public funds are distributed fairly and effectively, and that funds
have been managed in line with the Nolan Principles, Equality Act
2010, Public Sector Equality Duty and Managing Public Money
principles.”
 
The Authority as the
Neighbourhood Board’s Accountable Body will also be
responsible for ensuring that all funding is managed in accordance
with relevant public contract regulations including the Procurement
Act 2023.
 
MHCLG in its guidance expects
Neighbourhood Boards to publish a documented decision-making
process, for all papers going to Board meetings to be published in
advance of Board Meetings and for minutes to be published in
accordance with well-established local government
legislation.  The Authority as the
Accountable Body will be able to support the Board to meet those
requirements as well as its legal obligations referred to in the
report.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to allocate £1.5 billion UK Government funding to disadvantaged areas in Chirton and Percy Main and North Shields wards through the Pride in Place Programme.

purpose:
Agree the Housing and Property Annual
Complaints Performance and Service Improvement Report 2024-2025 and
its publication on the Authority's website.
content:
Cabinet received the Housing
and Property Services Annual Complaint Performance and Service
Improvement Report 2025-2026.  Cabinet
were advised that The Social Housing (Regulation) Act 2023 amended
the Housing Act 1916 and empowered the Housing Ombudsman (HO) to
issue a Complaint Handling Code (“the Code”) about
procedures for handling housing complaints to members of the
HO’s Scheme. As a social landlord, the Authority is by law a
member of the HO Scheme, which enables tenants, including those in
the social housing sector, to bring complaints against their
landlord using the Scheme. Cabinet were advised that a further
amendment to the Housing Act 1996 placed a duty on the HO to
monitor landlord compliance with the code.
 
Cabinet were advised that the
monitoring includes a requirement for landlords, such as the
Authority, to produce an Annual Complaints Performance and Service
Improvement Report.  This is to be
produced alongside the HO Annual Self-Assessment against the
Code.  The Authority’s
Self-Assessment is included as part of the Annual Complaints
Performance and Service improvement report appended to the
report.
 
Cabinet were advised that the
HO will monitor compliance in three ways to ensure that a
landlord:
 

·      
Has scrutinised and challenged the compliance with
the Code, complaints handling performance and learning from
complaints at its governing body and published the outcome on its
website;

·      
Complies with the Code in policy, and that any
deviations are explained and reasonable; and

·      
Complies with the Code in practice.
 
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to
 
(i)             
Agree the Housing and Property Services Annual
Complaints Performance and Service Improvement Report 2025-2026
appended to the report and to its publication on the
Authority’s website, and
(ii)            
Authorise the Director of Housing and Property
Services to submit the Housing Ombudsman’s Annual
Self-Assessment including in the Housing and Property Services
Annual Complaints Performance and Service Improvement Report
2025-2026 to the Housing Ombudsman.
 
Reason for the
decision:
 
The statutory Housing Ombudsman
Complaint Handling Code states that: ‘Landlords must produce
an annual complaints and service improvement report for scrutiny
and challenge.  The report must be
reported to the landlord’s governing body (or equivalent) and
published on its website alongside the governing body’s
repose to the report.’  The report
must be produced and published by 30 September 2026.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to agree to the Housing and Property Services Annual Complaints Performance and Service Improvement Report 2025-2026.

purpose:

content:
Cabinet received the Annual
Complaints Report 1 April 2025 – 31 March 2026 which provides
an overview of the complaints received by the Authority during this
period. 
 
Cabinet noted that listening to
residents and learning from their experiences is essential for the
Authority to deliver high-quality services and maintain the trust
of those it serves.  Cabinet noted that
the number of complaints the Authority receives each year continues
to be a very small proportion of the total number of transactions
and services delivered.  Cabinet were
advised that the Authority is committed to make sure that every
complaint is handled, fairly, consistently and in-line with the
principles of good complaint handling promoted by the Local
Government and Social Care Ombudsman and Housing
Ombudsman
 
Cabinet
RESOLVED
 
To agree the Annual
Complaints Report 1 April 2025 to 31
March 2026 appended to the report and it’s publication on the Authority’s
website.
 
Reason for the
Decision:
 
The reason for the decision is
that by presenting the report and the Annual Complaints Report 1
April 2025 – 31 March 2026 to Cabinet as the
Authority’s ‘Governing Body’, the Authority is
complying with the Housing Ombudsman’s Complaint Handling
Code and the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman’s
Complaint Handling Code.

report providing an overview of both service performance and the
financial position for 2026/27 across the Authority as at 30 June

impacts in budgetary terms, and showed the forecast outturn
position to 31 March 2027 for both revenue and capital.

finance and Treasury Management as at 30 June 2026, and

and the receipt of £2,536m of capital grants, and

the current level of financial pressures faced by the public
sector.  It is also important that

Authority as referred to in the report.

purpose:
Receive and approve the Authority’s
Final Plan for Change; an Authority wide approach to change to
support delivery of the Our North Tyneside Plan and Medium-Term
Financial Plan (MTFP).
content:
Cabinet were presented with a
report presenting the Authority’s ‘A Plan for
Change’ (“the Plan”). 
This is an organisation wide approach to creating and delivering
change that ensures delivery of high quality, sustainable outcomes
for residents, communities and businesses, as set out in the
Council Plan 2025-2029.
 
The report advised Cabinet that
the Authority has a proven track record of delivering high quality
and valued services to residents, however, like most local
authorities, it is facing key challenges around demand for
services, the cost of delivering those services, changing
population needs and a shift in customer expectations.  The plan provides an organisation-wide framework
and collective approach for delivering change.  It provides a set of strategic intentions that
will direct how the Authority will change over the period of the
Council Plan; these strategic intentions are:
 

·      
Increased focus on customer driven
delivery

·      
Refreshed delivery models

·      
A clear focus on services, not just
buildings

·      
A strong and embedded performance driven
culture

·      
A sharp commercial focus; and

·      
A continued culture of belonging and trust for
all.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to
 
Note and agree ‘A Plan
for Change’ as appended to the report.
 
Reason for the
Decision:
 
‘A Plan for Change’
appended to the report, has been developed using the feedback and
experience of customers, colleagues, Trade Unions and Elected
Members, as well as being subject to independent challenge for the
Local Government Association (LGA) Corporate Peer Challenge in
March 2026 and Chartered Institute of Public Finance and
Accountancy (CIPFA).  The feedback and
experiences have clarified the Authority’s approach to change
making sure it is understood and creates a shared sense of
purpose.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve 'A Plan for Change' to deliver high quality, sustainable outcomes for residents, communities, and businesses.

purpose:
Request to move to Pre-publication
consultation with interested parties regarding the future use of
the building, which will become vacant at the end of the 25/26
academic year - August 2026
content:
Cabinet received a report to
seek approval to commence a pre-publication consultation on a
proposal to relocate the primary aged pupils of Silverdale School
(“the School”) currently
located at the Langdale Centre, Wallsend into the Forest Hall
Primary School site at Delaval Road, Forest Hall when it becomes
vacant.
 
Cabinet were advised that the
proposal aims to:
 

·      
Enhance educational provision for pupils at the
School with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
(SEND);

·      
Make effective use of a vacant school site;
and

·      
Support sufficiency and suitability of specialist
provision across the Borough.
 
Cabinet were advised that
pre-publication consultation would enable full and proper
engagement with families, school teams and other stakeholders, to
inform the development of a potential statutory
proposal.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 
(i)             
Agree to the commencement of a pre-publication
consultation with parents/carers, staff, governing bodies,
local residents and other stakeholders
on the proposal to relocate the Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 pupils
of Silverdale School, from the Langdale Centre, Langdale Gardens to
the Forest Hall Primary School site at Delaval Road, Forest
Hall;
(ii)            
Authorise the Director of Children’s Services
in consultation with the Director of Housing and Property Services
and the Cabinet Member for Education, Inclusion, Employment and
Skills to:
a.    
Consider the responses received during
pre-publication consultation period; and
b.    
Determine whether to proceed to Statutory
consultation in accordance with Department for Education (DfE)
guidance.
(iii)          
Agree that should the Director of Children’s
Services in consultation with the Director of Housing and Property
Services and the Cabinet Member for Education, Inclusion,
Employment and Skills, determine that there should be statutory
consultation with the Schools,
parents/carers, the governing body and other stakeholders, the
Director of Children’s Services will present a further report
to Cabinet on the outcome of the statutory consultation and
determine next steps.
 
Reason for the
Decision:
 
This will enable the Authority
to explore options that may address the known challenges faced by
Silverdale School because of being located
in the Langdale Centre and the possibility of it being able
to move to a more suitable site.  The
recommendations also supports SEND
sufficiency and schools improvement, ensuring that such provision
remains sustainable and appropriate for local need.  The recommendations will also enable engagement
with parents/carers, staff and other stakeholders who would be part
of the development of the proposal.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to commence a pre-publication consultation on the proposal to relocate primary aged pupils of Silverdale School to the Forest Hall Primary School site.

twelve museums and galleries across North East England and the
Archives for Tyne and Wear.

their trading governance by replacing the separate
entities TWAMe and EBT with a single, combined company North East
Museums Ltd.  This will ensure that NEM

shareholder agreement.

officer Delegated Decision for North Tyneside Council as a
shareholder of NEM to the proposed changes.

the purchase of the property under RED80 of the Officer Delegation

Resources, the Elected Mayor, the Cabinet Member for Regeneration

delegation as set out in the Authority’s Financial

The Grant will be used to deliver a transport scheme at the

alterations to the existing crossing facilities and road widening
to create a bus lane on the exit at the roundabout from West Moor,
heading southbound towards Quorum Business Park, which will assist
the reliability of local bus services.

The works will be delivered through the Authority’s
partnership with Capita for the delivery of transport
schemes.

content:
Members received a presentation
commencing the discussion around work programming for the Green
Sub-Committee for the 2026-27 municipal year.
 
Members were informed that, to
enable effective preparation, a long list of potential topics for
scrutiny had been developed. Members were advised that, if
additional topics were identified for scrutiny throughout the year,
they could submit a suggestion sheet. Members were asked to
complete the suggestions sheets as fully as possible to strengthen
the reports provided to the sub
committee.
 
Members heard that Task and
Finish Groups could be established, if a topic was identified that
required a greater depth investigation. Task and Finish Groups do
not need to be decided at the start of the municipal year, rather
as the work programme progresses throughout the course of the
year.
 
Members were invited to suggest
items to be included on the work programme.
 
Members requested an update
during the next municipal year on Tree Management. Officers advised
that the tree management team were currently being restructured.
Once this process was completed, they could provide an update on
Tree Management.
 
Members also requested an
update on Highway and Transportation Delivery.

purpose:
To approve the content of the North Tyneside
Climate Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan.
content:
Cabinet were presented with the North Tyneside Climate
Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan. Cabinet were advised that the Strategy and Action Plan
builds on the learning from our
involvement in DEFRA’s Adaptation Pilot in 2024, and the work
which was undertaken with a wide range of local stakeholders
throughout 2025.  The Authority will
continue to engage with communities, partners and the voluntary
sector, Cabinet were advised that this will be central to
strengthening our resilience and ensuring the approach reflects
local needs and priorities.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 
(i)           
Note the content of this report;
(ii)         
Approve the Climate Adaptation Strategy and Action
Plan 2026-2029; and
(iii)        
Agree that a progress report will be presented to
Cabinet in 2029 on the Authority’s and the
Borough’s preparedness for the impacts of climate
change.
 
Reason for the decision:
 
Agreeing the recommendations
set out in paragraph 1.2 of the report will support
the delivery of the Authority’s Climate Adaptation
policy and develop a programmed approach with key stakeholder
groups.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the North Tyneside Climate Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan 2026-2029.

content:
Note the Performance and Financial position and note the update
on the budget and performance measures of each Service to 31
January 2026 and agree any recommendations that may be required
(depending on the outcome of the monitoring exercise).
 

Cabinet received an update on
the current position in relation to the key areas of performance
across the Authority as at 31 January 2026.
 
Cabinet were advised that
further detail on performance is contained within Annex 1 to the
report.
 
Cabinet were advised that
whilst there continues to be significant pressures in 2025/26 and
into the medium term, the Authority is continuing to see sustained
pressure across Adults’ and Children’s Social
Care.
 
Cabinet were advised that many
of the pressures in the current year are consistent with those
faced in recent years and, importantly, form part of the
Authority’s existing Medium Term Financial Plan
projects.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 
(i)       
Note the update provided on the Performance of the
Authority including updated data on the key pressures facing the
Authority;
(ii)      
Note the forecast budget monitoring position for the
General Fund, Housing Revenue Account, schools finance and Treasury
Management as at 31 January 2026 (sections 1.5.1, 1.5.2, 1.5.3 and
1.5.5 of the report);
(iii)     
Note the Authority’s Investment Plan spend of
£58.187m to 31 January 2026 and the proposed financing of the
Plan to the end of the year (as set out in Annex 2, Section 4 and
Appendix 1);
(iv)     
Approve reprogramming of £6.897m of the
2025/26 investment plan into future years and variations of
£2.553m within the 2025-2030 Investment Plan (section 1.5.4
of this report) and notes the current position with
Developers’ Contributions (section 1.5.6 of the
report);
(v)      
Approve the receipt of £0.045m new revenue
grants, and approves the receipt of £0.163m new capital
grants (as outlined in section 1.5.7 of the report);
(vi)     
Approve the write-offs of unrecoverable debt (as set
out in Annex 2, Section 1, 1.8.6).
 
Reason for the
Decision
 
It is important that Cabinet
continues to monitor performance against the Budget, especially
given the current level of financial pressures faced by the public
sector. It is also important that Cabinet agrees to receive the
revenue and capital grants referred to in the report.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to review the Authority's performance and financial position, approving reprogramming of investment plans and receipt of new grants.

in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Supporting and
Protecting Children, the Director of Resources and the Head of Law
to take all necessary steps to deliver a new 6-bed children’s
home for children with complex needs at Benton Lane, Longbenton,
subject to the granting of the necessary planning approval and the
obtaining of any other necessary requirements to enable the
children’s home to be delivered;
(iii)     
Authorise the Director of Children’s Services
in consultation with the Director of Resources and the Head of Law,
(subject to the granting of the necessary planning approval) to
enter into an agreement with the contracted builder to build the
children’s home to the Authority’s specifications and
to deal with all ancillary matters relating to the delivery of the
children’s home, including, but not limited to, obtaining
Ofsted registration of the home.
 
Reason for the decision:
 
It allows the necessary steps
to be taken by the Authority to deliver on the Authority’s
organisational objectives of directly delivering better care for
children in its care and of keeping more children who require
children’s home care arrangements in the Borough, close to
where they call home. The opportunity also has the potential to
deliver projected savings of £1.598m per annum to the
Authority.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to develop a new Council-owned Children's Home for children with complex needs at Benton Lane, aiming to provide better care for children and potential savings for the Authority.

purpose:

Plan prior to approval by the Health and Wellbeing Board and
submission to Department of Health and Social Care by 30 April
2026.
content:
Cabinet received a report in
relation to the Better Care Fund Plan for 2026-27.  Cabinet were advised that this pooled budget
arrangement provides funding to support integrated services across
health, social care and housing.
 
Cabinet were advised that the
detailed planning guidance and templates were not available in time
for this meeting so delegated authority is sought for the Director
of Adult Services in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Adult
Social Care and the Chair of the Health and Wellbeing Board to
approve the Better Care Fund Plan.
 
Cabinet were advised that there
is a strong link between the Better Care Fund and the Joint Health
and Wellbeing Strategy which is being refreshed for 2026 to
2030.  Evidence shows that joined up
systems can support the ambition for residents to live better lives
and a key focus if the impact on reducing inequalities for the most
vulnerable residents.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 
(i)       
Authorise the Director of Adult Services, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, the
Cabinet Member for Public Health and the Chair of the Health and
Wellbeing Board to agree the Better Care Fund Plan 2026/27 and
Planning Templates prior to the submission of the submission Better
Care Fund Plan to the Department of Health and Social Care;
and
(ii)      
Authorise the Director of Adult Services, in
consultation with the Director of Resources and Head of Law to
enter into an Agreement under section 75 of the National Health
Service Act 2006 and to implement the financial and administrative
arrangements for the Better Care Fund.
 
Reasons for the Decision:
 
The continuation of the BCF
presents an opportunity to take forward the principles of the
Health and Wellbeing Strategy and the Neighbourhood Health
agenda.  If the requirement to submit a
BCF Plan by 19 May 2026 and for the Authority to have entered into
a Section 75 Agreement following national approval of the Plan is
not achieved, the release of funds by the DHSC to the Authority
could be delayed.
 
The proposed delegations in the
report will enable the Director of Adult Services, following
appropriate consultation, to approve the BCF Plan and then enter
into the required Section 75 Agreement.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Better Care Fund Plan for 2026-27, providing funding for integrated health, social care, and housing services.

purpose:
To approve delegated authority to Director of
Housing, Director of Public Health and Director of Resources to
exercise all powers and duties under the provisions of the Renters
Rights Act 2025. To develop and keep updated any policy in relation
to the powers under the Renters’ Rights Act 2025.
content:
Cabinet were presented with a
report to seek the appropriate delegations and powers to enable the
Authority to take effective enforcement action and to introduce
policies required to fully implement the newly enacted Renters
Rights Act.
 
Cabinet were also advised that
the act represents a significant step forward in strengthening the
rights of private renters, providing them with greater security and
protection so that they can live in safe, good-quality homes for
longer without fear of unfair treatment.
 
The Act places new duties on
the Authority to enforce a wide range of potential breaches
committed by a landlord.  Cabinet were
advised that there will be a national awareness campaign to
accompany the rollout of the Act.  This
will be supported locally so that renters in North Tyneside will
understand their new rights and landlords are aware of their
responsibilities.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 
(i)    
authorise the Director of Public Health and the
Director of Housing and Property Services to exercise all powers
and duties under the provisions of the Renters’ Rights Act
2025 and for the Officer Delegation Scheme to be amended
accordingly as soon as reasonably practicable;
(ii)  
approve the Private Rented Enforcement Policy
attached at Appendix 1 of the report and the Private Rented Civil
Penalty Policy attached at Appendix 2;
(iii)authorise the Director of
Public Health and the Director of Housing and Property Services to
develop future Polices and Guidance relating the Renters’
Rights Act 2025, including, but not limited to, the enforcement of
the Act as considered appropriate in consultation with the Cabinet
member for Community Safety and the Climate Emergency, Director of
Housing and the Director of Resources and Head of Law;
and
(iv)authorise the Director of Public Health and Director of Housing
and Property Services to keep the Policies and Guidance referred to
in recommendations (ii) and (iii) above under review and to be
responsible for all matters relating to the Policies and Guidance,
including, but not limited to, making amendments to the Policies
and Guidance in consultation with the Cabinet member for Community
Safety and the Climate Emergency, Cabinet Member for Housing, the
Director of Resources and the Head of Law.
 
Reason for the Decision:
 
By making appropriate
delegations the Authority will be able to enforce the provisions of
the Act and to take action should breaches be found. This decision
ensures that the Authority can meet its statutory duties under
section 107 of the Act when it is implemented. The Policies
referred to in recommendations 2 and 3 of paragraph 1.2 of the
report will provide a clear and consistent framework for
enforcement decision making and as stated will support alignment
with the Act and national Guidance.
 
This decision minimises risk of
legal challenge, ensures that the Authority is implementing the Act
effectively and that the intended tenant protections are driven
forward. 
 
This decision provides the most
robust, legally compliant, and consistent approach to enforcement
under the Act, while allowing for managed transition and alignment
with national best practice.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to implement the Renters' Rights Act 2025, enhancing protections for private renters and enforcing new duties on landlords.

content:
Cabinet received a report from
the Green Sub-committee’s Task and Finish Group in relation
to parking on grass verges across the Borough.
 
Cabinet were advised that the work was undertaken following
a motion considered by Full Council in March 2025 which highlighted
concerns about indiscriminate parking on grass verges and the
resulting impact on neighbourhoods, safety and the local
environment.
 
Cabinet were advised that the Task and Finish Group met on
several occasions during 2025, gathering evidence, analysing the
scale and nature of the issue, and reviewing approaches taken by
other local authorities.  The process
has resulted in a clear set of findings and ten recommendations
which have been endorsed by the Overview and Scrutiny Co-ordination
and Finance Committee.
 
Cabinet are being asked to
consider the recommendations within the Task and Finish
Group’s report and agree that a formal response will be
brought forward to the May 2026 Cabinet meeting, which will set out
what action the Authority proposes to take.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 
(i)       
Consider the findings and recommendations of the
Overview and Scrutiny, Co-ordination and Finance Committee’s
Green Sub-Committee’s Task and Finish Group set out in its
Grass Verges Report of 28 January 2026 appended to this report at
Appendix 1, and; 
(ii)      
Agree that at its meeting in May 2026 Cabinet will
provide a formal response to the findings and recommendations of
the Overview and Scrutiny, Co-ordination and Finance
Committee’s Green Sub-Committee’s Task and Finish Group
report at Appendix 1 and indicate what action, if any, Cabinet
proposes to take in relation to those findings and
recommendations. 

 

Reason for the decision:

 
As the Overview and Scrutiny,
Co-ordination and Finance Committee has given notice that it
requires Cabinet to consider the report and recommendations of the
Green Sub-Committee, Cabinet is required to provide a response to
the recommendations within two months of receipt of the report, in
accordance with requirements of the Local Government Act
2000.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations on parking on grass verges, with a formal response to be provided in May 2026.

purpose:
The Governing Body of the school is expected
to meet on 23 February 2026 to consider the outcome of the
statutory consultation undertaken by the school to extend its age
range from Years 5-8 to Years 5-11. Under the applicable
legislation, Cabinet is required to consider the proposal made by
the Governing Body within two months of the close of the statutory
consultation, which closes on 22 February 2026.

Depending on a proposal being made by the Governing Body to extend
the age range, Cabinet will consider whether to approve or reject
this proposal.
content:
Cabinet were presented with a
report to consider, whether, as the statutory decision maker, to
approve the proposal to extend the age range of Monkseaton Middle
School from Year 5-8 to Year 5-11.
 
Cabinet were advised that a
full statutory process and consultation has been
undertaken.  Cabinet were also advised
that the proposal sits within the wider Strategic Education
Review.  The Governing Body and Local
Authority Officers have confirmed that the proposal is financially
viable and that a broad and balanced curriculum can be
delivered.
 
Cabinet were advised that this
proposal is seen as a less disruptive and more inclusive
alternative to school closure, particularly for pupils with SEND
and for families who value continuity of provision.
 
Cabinet
RESOLVED to:
 
(i)          
Consider the responses and the analysis of the
responses received by Monkseaton Middle School to its published
proposal which were received during the statutory representation
period between 26 January 2026 and 22 February 2026 appended to the
report at Appendix 7;
(ii)         
Note the responses to the pre-publication
consultation appended to the report at Appendix 3; and
(iii)        
Approve the published proposal to extend the age
range of pupils at Monkseaton Middle School without
modification.
 
Reason for the decision:
 
The proposal responds to
identified unmet need for smaller, more personalised secondary
phase provision and supports parental choice by enabling pupils to
remain in a familiar and inclusive setting through to Key Stage 4.
Consultation responses indicated clear community demand for a
mainstream alternative to larger secondary schools, particularly
for pupils who may struggle in those environments.


Potential impacts on neighbouring schools and the three-tier system
were carefully considered. Governors had reviewed pupil flow and
place planning evidence, which indicated that any impact on
surrounding schools would be limited, particularly in the context
of existing demand pressures and oversubscription at local high
schools. The objection received did not demonstrate a material
negative impact sufficient to outweigh the benefits of the
proposal.

The consultation process demonstrated overall support for the
proposal, including from headteachers within the Whitley Bay
pyramid. Governors emphasised that the substance and themes of
responses, rather than the number alone, supported progression of
the proposal. In particular, responses highlighted strong support
for maintaining a mainstream, inclusive school offer, the benefits
of educational continuity through to Key Stage 4, and the
importance of providing a smaller, more personalised learning
environment for pupils who may struggle in larger secondary
settings.
 
Alternative suggestions for the
school to become a specialist or alternative provision were
considered and discounted. Governors concluded that the proposed
age range extension best reflects the expressed wishes of the local
community for a mainstream, inclusive school and avoids excluding
pupils the proposal is intended to support.
 
The school leadership and
governing body would remain responsible for setting and managing
the school’s budget.  The
financial implications of the proposal had been modelled by the
school in detail, with support from Authority Officers, and had
been confirmed as viable, with assurance that a broad and balanced
curriculum can be delivered in line with DfE
expectations.
 
This information provide in
respect of the proposal had been reviewed by the Authority’s
Director of Resources who had provided confidence that the school
can sustainably operate across the extended age range. 
 
Based on the assumptions used,
year one (ending August 2028) would see an in-year deficit of
£0.118m, before moving into surplus of £0.084m in year
two and £0.233m in year three. 
 
The proposal also avoids the
costs that would arise if the school were to close, for example
retention and redundancy payments, which the school has estimated
could be in excess of £0.800m.
 
It should be noted that in line
with all school budgets, the number of pupils on roll is the key
determinant in the Local Funding Formula, which follows the
National Funding Formula, when assessing the main income stream for
any mainstream school.  Therefore, these
forecasts are not without risk, as the income is largely dependent
on pupil numbers in future years, but do demonstrate a financially
viable outcome based on the assumptions used.
 
The Governing Body was
satisfied that the required statutory processes, consultation
arrangements and due diligence had been followed appropriately. No
issues were identified that would prevent the proposal from
progressing to determination by Cabinet.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to extend the age range of Monkseaton Middle School to Year 5-11, providing a more inclusive alternative to school closure.

content:
Cabinet was provided with a
report to provide an update on the gathering of evidence in
relation to small HMOs.  The report
sought appropriate delegations to enable necessary steps to be
taken at the conclusion of the exercise.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 
(i)       
Note the update on the gathering of evidence
relating to Houses in Multiple Occupation in the Borough;
and
 
(ii)      
Authorise the Director of Regeneration and Economic
Development in consultation with the Deputy Mayor and Head of Law,
based on the evidence available on conclusion of the evidence
gathering, to determine whether or not to make a Direction under
Article 4(1) of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted
Development) (England) Order 2015 withdrawing the permitted
development right to change the use of a property from a dwelling
house (Use Class C3) to a small House in Multiple Occupation (Use
Class C4)  as set out in Class L(b) of
Part 3 of Schedule 2 to the Town and Country Planning (General
Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 in relation to changes
of use from Use Class C3 to Use Class C4 (as defined in the Town
and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 for specified areas
of the Borough; and
 
(iii)     
Note that if the Director of Regeneration and
Economic Development makes an Article 4 Direction, authorise him to
take all necessary steps in order for such a Direction to be made
and for him to subsequently confirm any such Direction in
accordance with Schedule 3 of the Town and Country Planning
(General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 including
sending appropriate notices to the Secretary of State.
 
Reason for the decision:
 
If there is robust evidence of
a concentration of HMOs in certain areas of the Borough and this is
having a detrimental impact on the amenity of these neighbourhoods,
eroding the sustainability and cohesion of communities, this is an
appropriate basis on which to introduce additional control. There
is limited control under the HMO licencing regime for some small
HMOs and such properties are currently not subject to any local
planning control. An appropriate form of control could be the
making of an Article 4 Direction relating to the specific locations
where there is evidence of harm from a concentration of
HMOs.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to gather evidence and potentially introduce additional control over small Houses in Multiple Occupation in certain areas of the Borough.

purpose:
Cabinet to consider the outcome
of the statutory consultation and determine next steps.
content:
Cabinet to consider the outcome
of the statutory consultation and determine next steps.
 

Cabinet received a
report regarding the Strategic Education
Review
Update – Proposal to
merge Hazlewood Primary School and Greenfields Primary School. This
report provided Cabinet with the consultation responses to the
statutory consultation on the merger of Hazlewood Primary School
and Greenfields Primary School, with the proposal to close
Hazlewood Primary School and use Greenfields Primary School to
accommodate the combined pupils. This
report contained the data and analysis for the
consultation responses received between 4 December 2025 and 21
December 2025. 
 
Cabinet received a further
supplementary report which contained the data and
analysis for the consultation responses received between 22
December 2025 and the close of the consultation at 5.00pm on 1
January 2026. 
 
Cabinet was informed that the
ambition for the Authority is to maintain a
sustainable, sufficient and high-quality education system
in North Tyneside, one that allows all children and young people to
achieve the best possible outcomes, including those
with additional needs. 
 
Cabinet was informed that a
rigorous and robust consultation process had taken place and every
view expressed had been listened to and carefully considered.
Cabinet recognised the passion the community has displayed for
their schools and expressed gratitude for the time and effort taken
by those who had shared their views with the
Authority. 
 
Cabinet acknowledged that the
decision was extremely difficult
but indicated that it was one that is
considered necessary to achieve an educationally and financially
sustainable education system in this part of the
Borough.  Cabinet
also indicated that the impact on the school
communities, including pupils and staff, was not
underestimated. It was noted that if the
decision was taken to merge the two schools, the
Authority would continue to work with the Leadership
of the schools, to ensure that the transition to the
merged school was as smooth as possible. 
During discussion on this
item a number of questions
were raised by Cabinet and responded to by the Cabinet Member for
Education, Inclusion, Employment and Skills.  It was explained that: 
 

An implementation
period up to September 2028 for the merger was being proposed and
this was longer than that originally suggested. This was in
response to the strength of feeling expressed during the
consultation and the potential for exploration of
academisation.  Discussions with a
potential academy sponsor were not sufficiently advanced to
entirely pause the process but the extended implementation period
would allow this option to continue to be
explored.

 

The structural
problems with the building on the Hazlewood Primary School site
meant that the site was not sustainable in the longer term. The
Authority had spent £2.5 million on temporary solutions and
had lobbied the Department for Education for financial support but
no additional funding had been allocated.

 

The impact of the
merger on students and staff was acknowledged and confirmed that
school leaders and education services would work together
to ensure that the transition was thoughtful and inclusive for
every child.

 

The Greenfields
Primary School site has capacity to ensure all pupils would have a
place in the merged school.

 

Greenfields Primary
School building, in common with many schools of that
era, contains asbestos in some areas and this is managed
by the school, with appropriate remedial action
taken.

 
Cabinet RESOLVED to approve the
proposal to merge Hazlewood Primary School and Greenfields Primary
School without modification, as per the implementation timetable
referred to in the full statutory proposal. 
 
Reason for the
DECISION: 
 
The Authority keeps under
review the number of pupils attending each school and updates
information each year about how many pupils are likely to be
attending schools in the future. This is an important aspect of the
Authority’s function in planning school places across the
Borough to ensure there are schools of a suitable size to meet
local requirements and to provide the best possible education for
the pupils they serve.
 
The Authority recognises that
school reorganisation of this nature will be of concern for local
communities, however, the current position is not sustainable.
Taking this into account, these proposals enable the Borough to
have a system of education that will bring about the highest
possible standards of education for all
of the children of North Tyneside for the short,
medium, and long term.
 
During the period of
pre-publication consultation and statutory representation,
no viable alternatives or options were presented, though
all were carefully considered.
 
Through the merger there would
be sufficient capacity to accommodate pupils now and to meet
the likely future demand for places in the medium and
long term. It is proposed that full implementation will take place
from September 2028.
 
As part of the consultation,
there were a number
of responses which addressed the implementation
approach that would be adopted if the proposal was taken
forward. The benefits of a delayed implementation period,
particularly in relation to managing existing and new sibling
links, reduction in the number and size of ‘bulge’ year
groups and facilitating any building adaptations, were
considered. It was considered that, if the decision to move forward
was taken, there would be a later implementation date (September
2028) than the indicative date included in the pre-publication
consultation documentation. However, if it became appropriate to do
so the Authority would consider accelerating the
implementation plans ahead of
the September 2028 date.
This delayed implementation
would also allow Hazlewood Primary School to explore further an
approach that has been made to join a Multi Academy Trust. It is
too early to conclude whether this is a viable option,
especially given the building issues at Hazlewood Primary School.
The Authority does not have the powers to action this proposal, and
this is not something that the Authority can mandate schools to
do.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the merger of Hazlewood Primary School and Greenfields Primary School, with an extended implementation period up to September 2028.

purpose:
To agree the number of Band D Equivalent Properties in the
Council Tax Base.  To agree the long
term Council Tax collection rate, which is used as part of the
Council Tax Base calculation
content:
To agree the number of Band D Equivalent Properties in the
Council Tax Base.  To agree the long
term Council Tax collection rate, which is used as part of the
Council Tax Base calculation
 

Cabinet was presented with a
report on the proposed Council Tax Base for 2026/27.
 
Cabinet was advised that the
Council Tax Base is a statutory calculation that was used in the
2026/27 Budget and Council Tax setting process. Cabinet was also
advised that it is used as the basis for our major precepting
authorities, the Police and Crime Commissioner for Northumbria and
the Tyne and Wear Fire and Rescue Authority.
 
Cabinet was asked to note, the
2026/27 Council Tax Base calculation takes into
account one change, to introduce a banded Council Tax
Reduction Scheme for working age claimants, which was approved by
Council on 27 November 2025. Cabinet was advised that this change
meant that we could target support to the most financially
vulnerable residents and is part of the strategy to reduce poverty.
Cabinet was advised that the report also included the latest
estimated forecast of property growth in the Borough.
 
Cabinet was also asked to
determine the assumed long term collection rate for Council Tax.
Cabinet was advised that this had been set at 98.5% since 2013/14,
with only a reduction in collection rate to 98% in 2021/22 in
recognition of the difficult financial situation that many
households were in due to the Covid 19 Pandemic.
 
Cabinet was informed that
whilst collection remains challenging, the in-year performance is
in line with what was achieved at the same point in the previous
year. It was suggested to Cabinet that the assumed long term
collection rate of 98.5% set in the previous year remains
achievable.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 

1.    
Approve the report on the calculation of North
Tyneside’s Council Tax Base for 2026/27; and

2.    
Agree that the assumed long term Council Tax
collection rate for 2026/27 is set at 98.5% and therefore the
amount calculated by North Tyneside Council as its Council Tax Base
for 2026/27 will be 65,439 Band D equivalent properties, pursuant
to the report and in accordance with the Local Authorities
(Calculation of Council Tax Base) (England) Regulations
2012.
 
Reason for the
DECISION:
 
The risk of setting a Council
Tax collection rate too high is that this can result in a deficit
position for the Council Tax element of the Collection Fund, which
in turn will have to be funded by the Authority’s General
Fund.
 
This collection rate is
reviewed as part of the annual Council Tax Base calculation, and
the 98.5% collection rate will be reviewed in determining the
Council Tax Base for 2026/27.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Council Tax Base for 2026/27 and set the long term Council Tax collection rate at 98.5%.

purpose:
Cabinet to consider the outcome of the
statutory consultation and determine next steps.
content:
Cabinet received a
report regarding the Strategic Education
Review
Update – Proposal to
merge Ivy Road Primary School and Forest Hall Primary School. This
report provided Cabinet with the consultation responses to the
statutory consultation on the merger of Ivy Road Primary School and
Forest Hall Primary School, with the proposal to close Ivy Road
Primary School and use the Ivy Road School site
to relocate Forest Hall Primary School to accommodate the
combined pupils. This report contained the data and
analysis for the consultation responses received between 4 December
2025 and 21 December 2025.
 
Cabinet received a further
supplementary report which contained the data and
analysis for the consultation responses received between 22
December 2025 and the close of the consultation at 5.00pm on 1
January 2026.
 
Cabinet was informed that the
ambition of the Authority is to maintain a
sustainable, sufficient and high-quality education system
in North Tyneside, one that allows all children and young people to
achieve the best possible outcomes, including those
with additional needs.
 
Cabinet was informed that a
rigorous and robust consultation process had taken place and every
view expressed had been listened to and carefully
considered. 
 
Cabinet recognised the passion
the community has displayed for their schools and expressed
gratitude for the time and effort taken by those who had shared
their views with the Authority.
 
Cabinet acknowledged that the
decision was extremely difficult but indicated that it
was one that is considered necessary to achieve an educationally
and financially sustainable education system in this part of the
Borough. Cabinet also indicated that the impact on the
school communities, including pupils and staff, was not
underestimated.  It was noted that if
the decision was taken to merge the two schools, the
Authority would continue to work with the Leadership of the
schools, to ensure that the transition to the merged school was as
smooth as possible.  Cabinet noted the
challenges faced in this area which have led to the consideration
to merge Ivy Road Primary School and Forest Hall Primary School,
with Forest Hall Primary School retaining its Department
for Education (DfE) number but being based at the Ivy Road
site.
 
During discussion on this
item a number of questions
were raised by Cabinet and responded to by the Cabinet Member for
Education, Inclusion, Employment and Skills. It was explained
that: 
 

The Ivy Road site has
more than enough space to accommodate the merged school. The Ivy
Road site is the larger of the two sites and has two assembly
halls, a large yard and playing field, car parking spaces and
bigger facilities. The Authority will work with the school to look
at the requirements and this
may include the redesignation of some spaces for the pupil
cohort for September 2026. The Authority would continue to work
with the school to ensure that the accommodation was appropriate
for a 1.5 form entry school for future admissions.

 

The implementation
period was considered appropriate as there are no other
options available for the schools and therefore it is preferable to
merge the schools quickly as this will provide greater stability
and prevent a financial deficit from continuing to grow. Both
schools have excellent staff and pupil welfare is a top
priority. 

 

During the transition
period the schools will ensure that pupils are looked after. The
school leadership and the Authority will work together. There will
not be a ‘one size fits all’ approach as transition
plans will be personalised. 

 
Cabinet RESOLVED to approve the proposal
to merge Ivy Road Primary School and Forest Hall Primary School,
without modification, as per the implementation timetable referred
to in the full statutory proposal. 
 
Reason for the
DECISION: 
 
The Authority keeps under
review the number of pupils attending each school and updates
information each year about how many pupils are likely to be
attending schools in the future. This is an important aspect of the
Authority’s function in planning school places across the
Borough to ensure there are schools of a suitable size to meet
local requirements and to provide the best possible education for
the pupils they serve.
 
The Authority recognises that
school reorganisation of this nature will be of concern for local
communities, however, the current position is not sustainable.
Taking this into account, these proposals enable the Borough to
have a system of education that will bring about the highest
possible standards of education for all
of the children of North Tyneside for the short,
medium, and long term. 
 
During the period of
pre-publication consultation and statutory representation,
no viable alternatives or options were presented, though
all were carefully considered.
 
Through the merger there would
be sufficient capacity to accommodate pupils now and to meet
the likely future demand for places in the medium and
long term. It is proposed that full implementation will take place
from September 2026.
 
The implementation date of
September 2026 would sustain high quality education in the
community, provide greater stability for all local pupils, improve
financial sustainability, and support the provision of a
high-quality education for everyone. If left unchanged, the risk is
that the two schools would continue to grow in deficit, and this in
turn would limit their ability to sustain high quality
education.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the merger of Ivy Road Primary School and Forest Hall Primary School to achieve a sustainable education system in North Tyneside.

purpose:

content:
For Cabinet to consider whether to make, publicise and consult on an Article 4 Direction to
introduce controls over small HMOs by removing permitted
development rights to change a dwelling into a small
HMO.

Cabinet received a report that
proposed the gathering of evidence in relation to Small Houses in
Multiple Occupation (HMOs) in the Borough.
 
Cabinet was informed that the
gathering of evidence would be used to ascertain if the number of
small Houses in Multiple Occupation in parts of the Borough
negatively impact on residential amenity, local character and
wellbeing of any area. Cabinet was advised that gathering of
evidence would help to inform whether there is a robust case to
take steps to introduce controls over the creation of small HMOs in
areas of the Borough. Cabinet was informed that such control could
be in the form of a Direction to remove the existing national
permitted development right which allows a small HMO to be created
without the need for planning permission.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 

1.    
Agree to the gathering of evidence on the number of
small Houses in Multiple Occupation in the Borough and the impact,
if any, on the local amenity, character and wellbeing of any areas
of the Borough through the number of and use of such properties;
and
 

2.    
Receive a further report following the completion of
the gathering of the evidence so that Cabinet can determine what
steps, if any, should be taken in relation to such properties,
including, but not limited to, controlling the number of such
properties through planning control.
 
Reason for the
DECISION:
 
In line with the requirements
of the National Planning Policy Framework, the gathering of
evidence with assist Cabinet in the making of any appropriate and
necessary future decisions.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to gather evidence on small HMOs and consider introducing controls over their creation.

content:
Cabinet received a report
setting out its response to the Overview and Scrutiny Co-ordination
and Finance Committee: Report from Secure Sub-Committee Task and
Finish Group on Anti-Social Behaviour.
 
Cabinet considered an initial
report at its meeting on 24 November 2025 from the task group which
was set up to review the processes and procedures in place to
tackle anti-social behaviour and support victims.
 
Cabinet received fourteen
recommendations from the Task and Finish Group, proposed responses
to the recommendations were presented to Cabinet for
approval.
 
Cabinet was asked to note that,
despite a significant reduction in Anti-Social Behaviour in the
Borough and increasing satisfaction from tenants in the annual
satisfaction survey, better never stops. Cabinet was advised that
many of the recommendations were implemented with immediate effect.
Cabinet was advised that, by the new financial year, it is hoped
that new policies and procedures will be in place on the back of
the recommendations, making North Tyneside an even safer place to
live.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 

1.    
Agree the proposed responses to the recommendations
made by the Overview and Scrutiny Co-ordination and Finance
Committee’s report from Secure Sub-Committee Task and Finish
Group on Anti-Social Behaviour; and
 

2.    
Authorise the Director of Housing and Property
Services and the Director of Resources to take all necessary steps
to deliver the proposed actions as they apply to each of their
respective Directorates.
 
Reason for the
DECISION:
 
This will allow the Authority
to progress the recommendations of the Task and Finish Group in
accordance with Cabinet’s wishes. This will also fulfil
Cabinet’s responsibility to formulate a response to the Task
and Finish Group’s report, in accordance with the
requirements of the Local Government Act 2000.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations on tackling anti-social behaviour in North Tyneside.

content:
Cabinet received the 2025/26
Performance and Financial Management Report, which provided Cabinet
with an overview of service performance and the financial position
across the Authority as at 30 November 2025.
 
Cabinet was informed that the
Authority had continued to experience comparatively low levels of
crime and anti-social behaviour. Cabinet was advised that support
for young people post-16 remained effective and that the level of
16–17-year-olds not in education, employment or training
remained low. The Affordable Homes Programme continued to stay on
track with 206 new affordable homes expected to be delivered in the
coming year.
 
Cabinet was advised that the
Authority continued to face significant financial challenges and
these were expected to continue into the medium term which Cabinet
had acknowledged in its initial budget proposals.  In common with other Local Authorities, the
Authority has continued to see sustained pressure across
Adults’ and Children’s Social Care.
 
Cabinet was informed that there
remained a forecast net pressure for the year of £6.2m.
Whilst clearly a significant challenge, this was an improved
position from the September Cabinet Report, and the Authority will
continue to take measures to improve this position
further.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 

1.    
Note the update provided on the Performance of the
Authority including updated data on the key pressures facing the
Authority;
 

2.    
Note the forecast budget monitoring position for the
General Fund, Housing Revenue Account, schools finance and Treasury
Management as at 30 November 2025;
 

3.    
Note the Authority’s Investment Plan spend of
£46.733m to 30 November 2025 and the proposed financing of
the Plan to the end of the year;
 

4.    
Approve reprogramming of £0.350m of the
2025/26 investment plan into future years and variations of
£2.907m within the 2025-2030 Investment Plan and notes the
current position with Developers’ Contributions;
 

5.    
Approve the receipt of £0.074m new revenue
grants; and
 

6.    
Approve the receipt of £0.762m of capital
grants.
 
Reason for the
DECISION:
 
It is important that Cabinet
continues to monitor performance against the Budget, especially
given the current level of financial pressures faced by the public
sector. It is also important that Cabinet agrees to receive the
revenue and capital grants referred to in the report.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations based on the 2025/26 Performance and Financial Management Report for the Authority.

purpose:
Consideration of revised
governance arrangements at Newcastle International
Airport.
content:
Consideration of revised
governance arrangements at Newcastle International
Airport.

Cabinet received a report
seeking approval to formally provide the Authority’s consent
to the disposal of Company A’s shares at an
appropriate meeting of that company.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED to: 
 
1.     
Approve the proposed sale by Company A of part of
its shares in the Newcastle International Airport Limited group
(NIAL) to Company B on the terms as described in
the report;

 
2.
  Authorise the Elected Mayor, as a
Director of Newcastle Airport Local Authority Holding Company
Limited (NALAHCL) (or in the Elected Mayor’s absence, the
Deputy Mayor as the Authority’s alternate Director of
NALAHCL), to provide the Authority’s consent to
recommendation 1 above at the relevant meeting of NALAHCL;
and
 
3.  Authorise the Head of Law in
consultation with the Director of Resources to agree and execute
all necessary legal agreements on behalf of the
Authority in order to give
effect to recommendation 1 above.
 
Reason for the
DECISION: 
 
Company A has informed
the 7 local authority shareholders of NIAL (“the
LA7”) that it wishes to dispose of a majority of its
shareholding in NIAL. Under the terms of the NIAL
Shareholders’ Agreement, the LA7 have the right to approve
the proposed disposal of shares by Company A. Acting in
consultation with the LA7, Company A has managed its sales process
in the private market and Company B has been identified as its
preferred bidder.  
 
It is considered by the LA7
that Company B would be a suitable fit as a new partner in the
ownership of NIAL based on a number of factors, including airport
experience, alignment of economic objectives and vision with the
LA7, previous background in working within public/private
partnerships and acceptance of the new partner of the terms of the
existing NIAL Shareholders’ Agreement. In addition, the
proposals will also lead to financial benefits for the LA7. It is
therefore considered that there is
no valid reason for the Authority and the LA7 to withhold their
consent to the proposed disposal by Company A
of the majority of its shares
in NIAL to Company B.
 
Cabinet was informed
that in accordance with the Authority’s
Constitution, written approval has been given by the
Authority’s Section 151 Officer, the Monitoring Officer and
the Chair of Council, that this decision is not subject to call-in
and may be implemented immediately.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the sale of shares in Newcastle International Airport Limited group to Company B.

purpose:
For Cabinet to note and approve
the 2025-29 Engagement Strategy.
content:
For Cabinet to note and approve
the 2025-29 Engagement Strategy.

Cabinet received a report
introducing the Resident Engagement Strategy 2026-2029 setting out
the Authority's approach to listening and working alongside
residents to shape its services and priorities. Cabinet was advised
that the strategy supports the ambitions of the Council Plan and
meets national standards for consultation and
engagement.
 
Cabinet was informed that the
vision is for residents to be informed, included and empowered
through open and meaningful engagement. There is a commitment to
act on resident feedback to improve services and strengthen
trust.
 
Cabinet was advised that the
strategy expands opportunities for residents to get involved, links
engagement to decision-making, and sets clear standards for
high-quality engagement across all service areas.
 
Cabinet was informed that
recent consultation with residents and colleagues had shaped the
strategy, ensuring it reflected to the needs and aspirations of
communities. Cabinet was advised that progress would be tracked and
reported annually and feedback would directly influence
services.
 
Cabinet RESOLVED
to:
 

1.    
Approve the Resident Engagement Strategy 2026-2029;
and
 

2.    
Note that the Authority will produce and publish an
annual Resident Engagement Report.
 
Reasons for the
DECISION:
 
The Strategy is shaped by
extensive experience and best practise, is guided by national
legislation, and has been developed in consultation with residents
to ensure it reflects their needs and aspirations.
 
It aligns with the principles
in the Council Plan 2025/2029 supporting early engagement,
empowering residents to help shape services, and tailoring
approaches to deliver the best possible outcomes for all
communities.
 
The Strategy is fully aligned
with the Authority’s Customer Promise, ensuring that the
Authority listens, understands, and acts on residents’ views,
provide clear and open communication, and use feedback to shape and
improve the services that matter most to communities.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the 2026-2029 Resident Engagement Strategy.
